name: semaphore-arm-cast
title: Semaphore Arm Cast
description: An ambient status indicator drawn as a Chappe optical telegraph mast: two pivoting arms swing to a new 45-degree angle pair every ~2.15s, each held pose reading as a distinct relayed symbol.
useWhen: an ambient status or multi-stage indicator should read as a mechanical relay handing off one discrete symbol at a time rather than a spinner or a swapped icon — two arms pivot on a fixed mast to a new held angle pair on a slow, unhurried cadence, legible from a glance the way a relay tower's held position was legible from the next tower down the line; pick status-glyph-cadence instead when the indicator has to sit inline beside a text label at 20-64px and encode five distinct TASK states (working/searching/awaiting-input/blocked/done) via motion cadence rather than cycle through an unbounded, state-agnostic ambient sequence — semaphore-arm-cast has no state prop and does not represent success/failure/waiting, it is pure ambient 'something is alive' motion, structurally a mast-and-pivot mechanism (not the wire-tension railway blade of semaphore-arm-tension).
instruction: An ambient card-scale SVG status indicator modeled on the Chappe optical telegraph (France, 1794): a vertical mast carries a horizontal regulator bar near its top, and a pivoting indicator arm is mounted at each end of the bar. Geometry is derived entirely from the container's smaller dimension, measured via getBoundingClientRect on mount and re-measured on every ResizeObserver callback: mastHeight = min(width,height) * 0.8, armLength = min(width,height) * 0.28, the regulator bar sits at 14% down from the mast's top and spans armLength * 1.8 centered on the mast, and both arms pivot from the bar's two endpoints. Each arm is an SVG <line> nested in a <g> whose transform is `rotate(angle pivotX pivotY)`, angle measured from straight-up (0deg) clockwise in 45deg increments (0/45/90/135/180/225/270/315deg) — 8 discrete positions per arm. A fixed 9-entry symbol table pairs one angle per arm per symbol; the component free-runs through it as an unbounded loop, one symbol at a time, index 3 fixed at (135deg, 270deg) as the widest asymmetric spread in the set. A single requestAnimationFrame loop accumulating real delta-time drives a two-phase clock per symbol: SWING phase is 700ms total — arm 1 begins an eased (cubic ease-in-out) 550ms rotation from its old angle to the new one immediately at phase start, arm 2 begins its own 550ms eased rotation 150ms later so the two arms visibly depart and arrive independently rather than in lockstep, matching a two-man relay — followed by a DWELL phase of 1.6s where both arms sit fully settled at the held pair before the next symbol's swing begins; full beat is 2.3s (550ms swing + 150ms stagger overlap + 1.6s dwell), 9-symbol loop is a ~20.7s full cycle. Both arm angles are recomputed directly from phase-elapsed time every frame (never a CSS transition triggered by a setTimeout), so an IntersectionObserver and the document visibilitychange listener can pause the rAF loop outright when off-screen or the tab is hidden and resume later mid-swing with zero re-trigger or jump. Mast, bar and both arms are stroke-only from var(--foreground) directly in inline SVG attributes (no JS color read needed since var() resolves and repaints on the theme class flip for free); arm stroke width is set to 1.8x the mast/bar stroke width specifically so the two moving arms never optically merge into the static mast at small card sizes or in light theme's flatter default contrast, and a small filled circle marks each pivot for the same reason. `prefers-reduced-motion` freezes on symbol index 3 (135deg / 270deg, both arms fully settled, no swing) permanently rather than the loop's t0 symbol, chosen because it is the most structured pose in the set — several other symbols place both arms close to vertical, which reads as at-rest rather than as an active signal. Pure SVG + rAF, zero dependencies, no canvas, no interaction (ambient only) — root is `role=img` with a static `aria-label` describing the mechanism rather than a live region, since the angle pairs carry no meaning to announce per-symbol.
